items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: So at that time I was working for an undertaker. His name was Elmer [Burns]. ... So he took me and showed me the positions on it, showed me how to put my lip on it and how to attack the notes

ctx.x: So he used to come home all the time, you know, come through Springfield, and he said, "Gee whiz, Quent," he said, "you've got such a good musical background, why don't you take the trombone? Because there's very few good colored trombone players. This would be a good instrument for you." So I thought over this thing and thought over this thing and finally the guys at home, my buddies, they got a band together and they had nine pieces. They needed a trombone to make ten pieces.

So at that time I was working for an undertaker. His name was Elmer [Burns]. I used to drive the ambulance and I used to play the organ for the funerals and things, you know, then jump out and drive the funeral car. And Elmer [Burns] had a brass trombone, he played in the Elks band. So I told Elmer, I said, "Elmer," I said, "why don't you tell me about this trombone? I'd like to know how it works and how do you play it. I'd like to know about this."
So he took me and showed me the positions on it, showed me how to put my lip on it and how to attack the notes,
